messages.subject: No Output for Logistic Regression in Rattle
parts:

else experienced this problem?

messages.subject: Re: No Output for Logistic Regression in Rattle
parts:
Hi Ernesto,

Thanks for the update.

I can reproduce the error on Windows. Still trying on GNU/Linux.

Under Windows, with R 6.2.1, the output from summary(crs$glm) includes
what looks like a unicode quote character in the Signif. codes
line. For some strange reason this is causing the display of the whole
text to fail!!!

Viz, the output looks like:

========================================================================

Call:
glm(formula = Adjusted ~ ., family = binomial(logit), data = [...]
c(2, 5, 7:10, 13)])

Deviance Residuals:
Min 1Q Median 3Q Max
-2.0806 -0.7002 -0.3141 -0.1701 2.7337

Coefficients:
Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)
(Intercept) -5.346e+00 5.205e-01 -10.271 < 2e-16 ***
Age 2.760e-02 6.563e-03 4.206 2.60e-05 ***

[...]

---
Signif. codes: 0 .***. 0.001 .**. 0.01 .*. 0.05 ... 0.1 . . 1

(Dispersion parameter for binomial family taken to be 1)

[...]

========================================================================

Before and after the ***, ** etc, in the "Signif. codes" line, there
are quote characters, that in my posting to this email have become "."
They seem to be unicode characters (the open quote is, in hexadecimal,
#x53978, and the close quote is #x53979).

When this string is displayed in the textbuffer in Rattle, it fails,
and does not display anything.

I'm not sure yet whether this is a result of this new version of R or
something has changed in the RGtk2 libraries.

Still investigating.

Regards,
Graham

messages.author: 51ea28fc190ac537
messages.subject: Re: No Output for Logistic Regression in Rattle
parts:
Hi Ernesto,

Michael Lawrence (author of RGtk2) has pointed me to the fact that R
has introduced some fancy quote handling:

Received Tue 27 Nov 2007 11:58pm +1100 from Michael Lawrence:
> Looks like this is the problem:
>
> o dQuote() and sQuote() are more flexible, with rendering
> controlled by the new option 'useFancyQuotes'. This includes
> the ability to have TeX-style rendering and directional quotes
> (the so-called 'smart quotes') on Windows. The default is to
> use directional quotes in UTF-8 locales (as before) and in the
> Rgui console on Windows (new).
>
>
>
> I wonder what his setting is for:
>
> options("useFancyQuotes")
>
> If you set it to "UTF-8" it should work as on Linux. The default locale
> ("C") locale on Windows does not use Unicode for the fancy quotes. UTF-8 is
> required by GTK+. This is a major annoyance.

A quick fix is to run the following in the R window:

> options(useFancyQuotes="utf8")

I'll wrap some function calls in Rattle with this so that inside
Rattle it should work okay (and outside of Rattle the option won't
change - not an ideal solution, but it should work for now).

Thanks again for the bug report.

Regards,
Graham
